text:
Barrett Hayton's season is the best kind of quiet: Utah takes 64.3% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, more than ten points better than without him. That's a top-of-the-league number for a center playing under 15 minutes a night.

The scoring is starting to catch up. He tied the game in the third against Vancouver on Nov. 16, scored on the power play to force overtime against San Jose two nights earlier, and has 4 goals and 13 points in 23 games. He's about a goal and a half under his chances, so there's room for more.

Five years after the Coyotes took him fifth overall (one pick after Brady Tkachuk), Hayton has never quite become a scorer, and last season Evolving-Hockey had him worth 0.3 wins, most of it from defense. What's different now is that Utah is creating with him on, not just surviving. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 1.5 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the high-percentage looks. Watch whether André Tourigny gives him more than 15 minutes.
